answer: A 233 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the prism index keeps every digest, the river audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, because the sonnet fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 12 dollars per alias.
